title: Architecture-preserving interfacial regulation via sulfonated graphene oxide for high-performance stretchable ionic thermoelectrics

segments.text: Stretchable ionic thermoelectric (i-TE) materials capable of simultaneously delivering high thermopower and mechanical compliance are essential for harvesting low-grade heat in deformable, self-powered human-machine interfaces.
In these systems, the electrical potential originates from the Soret-effect-driven asymmetric thermo-diffusion of ions.

However, conventional strategies typically rely on bulk polymer modifications to regulate this asymmetry, which inherently couples ionic transport with the host polymer's structural properties, thereby limiting the independent optimization of electrochemical and mechanical performance.
Here, we report a sulfonated graphene oxide (SGO)-mediated interfacial regulation strategy that modulates ionic transport without altering the host polymer framework.

The incorporation of SGO nanosheets provides immobilized anionic sites that significantly enhance ion-mobility asymmetry, while simultaneous hydrogen-bonding and ion-dipole interactions reinforce the polymer network.

When integrated into a polyacrylamide (PAM) network containing a deep eutectic solvent (DES), the resulting SGO-based eutectogel exhibits a high ionic Seebeck coefficient of 18.0 mV K-1, an ionic conductivity of 7.95 mS cm(-1), and a dimensionless figure of merit (zT(i)) of 0.71.
Beyond its TE performance, the eutectogel maintains 87% of its initial Seebeck coefficient even under 500% tensile strain and shows minimal degradation (<10%) after 500 deformation cycles.

The practical utility of this system was validated through a serialized 4 & times; 4 array module that successfully harvests low-grade waste heat from daily electronics to directly power a light-emitting diode and drive a small fan.
This design offers a structurally simple yet versatile platform for high-performance i-TE systems operating in mechanically dynamic environments.

title: Low-power biomimetic ionic thermoelectric device for multi-gas olfaction

segments.text: The escalating demand for intelligent multi-gas sensing has driven the need for high-performance artificial olfactory systems with enhanced power efficiency.

This work proposes an innovative gas sensing mechanism enabled by the giant ionic-thermoelectric effect in solid-state ionic polymer, which overcomes the low thermopower-to-thermal conductivity (S/kappa) limitation of the conventional thermoelectric materials.
Using wafer-scale microfabrication technology, we demonstrate the first functional ionic-thermoelectric biomimetic olfactory device that can simultaneously resolve mixed gas analytes.

This monolithic platform integrates multiple sub-100 mu m sensing units, each combining an ionic-thermoelectric module with a narrow-bandpass optical filter, to selectively resolve the contributions of individual gas species in mixed-gas environments.

The device achieves a record responsivity of 2340 V/W, a 20-fold improvement over commercial detectors (typically <200 V/W) and limits of detection of 1.42 ppm, 0.15 ppm, and 1.16 ppb for CO2, CH4 and CO, respectively.
This work establishes a promising route to next-generation artificial olfactory systems based on the ionic-thermoelectric effects.

reference.quote: Using wafer-scale microfabrication technology, we demonstrate the first functional ionic-thermoelectric biomimetic olfactory device that can simultaneously resolve mixed gas analytes.

reference.subject: Ionic-thermoelectric biomimetic olfactory device
reference.quote: Using wafer-scale microfabrication technology, we demonstrate the first functional ionic-thermoelectric biomimetic olfactory device that can simultaneously resolve mixed gas analytes.
context_quotes: This monolithic platform integrates multiple sub-100 mu m sensing units, each combining an ionic-thermoelectric module with a narrow-bandpass optical filter, to selectively resolve the contributions of individual gas species in mixed-gas environments.

reference.subject: Ionic-thermoelectric biomimetic olfactory device
reference.conditions: Reported as a record and a 20-fold improvement over commercial detectors, typically <200 V/W
reference.quote: Using wafer-scale microfabrication technology, we demonstrate the first functional ionic-thermoelectric biomimetic olfactory device that can simultaneously resolve mixed gas analytes.
context_quotes: The device achieves a record responsivity of 2340 V/W, a 20-fold improvement over commercial detectors (typically <200 V/W) and limits of detection of 1.42 ppm, 0.15 ppm, and 1.16 ppb for CO2, CH4 and CO, respectively.
